test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 17th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: During a flight of 900 km, an aircraft was slowed down due to bad weather. Its average speed for the trip was reduced by 300 km/h and the time of flight increased by 30 min. The original duration of the flight was :
solution:
**Given :**

Distance = 900 km

Average speed is reduced by 300 km/h 

Time of flight is increased by 30 min. 

**Concept used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Average speed = Total distance/Total time

**Calculation:**

Let the original time of flight be T hrs

So, original average speed = 900/T 

When average speed is reduced by 300 km/h and time of flight is increased by 30 min.

According to the question,

Reduced average speed = 900/T - 300

New time of flight = (T + 1/2) hrs

New average speed = 900/(T + 1/2)

Equating average speed, we get

⇒ (900/T) - 300 = 900/(T + 0.5)

⇒ (3/T) - 1 = 3/(T + 0.5)

⇒ (3 - T)/T = 3/(T + 0.5)

⇒ (3 - T)(T + 0.5) = 3T 

⇒ T² + 0.5T - 1.5 = 0

⇒ 2T² + T - 3 = 0

⇒ (T - 1)(2T + 3) = 0

⇒ T - 1 = 0 ⇒ T = 1 hr

**∴ The original time of flight is 1 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**In such type of problems, use the formula directly

(S1 × S2)/(S1 - S2) × Time difference (in hours) = Distance (in km)

where S1 and S2 are the initial and final average speeds (in km/hr)

⇒ Let original average speed be S km/hr

⇒ S × (S - 300)/300 × 1/2 = 900

⇒ S × (S - 300) = 900 × 600

⇒ On comparing, we can tell directly that S = 900 km/hr

∴ The original time of flight = 900/900 =** 1 hr.**
